issues.title: GFM protocol autolink starts right after `<`, linking URLs inside non-autolink angle brackets
issues.body:
**Marked version:** 18.1.1 **Markdown flavor:** GitHub Flavored Markdown (default) ## Description Same root cause as #4118, but for the `http://` / `https://` case, which is still reproducible on 18.1.1. No existing issue that I could find for the protocol variant. ## Expectation `` is not a CommonMark autolink (link destinations can't contain spaces), and a GFM extended autolink "can only come at the beginning of a line, after whitespace, or any of the delimiting characters `*`, `_`, `~`, and `(`" — `<` is not one of them. GitHub renders it as plain text: ```html

<https://example.com/foo bar>

``` ## Result ```js marked.parse('') ``` ```html

<https://example.com/foo bar>

``` The lexer emits a link token with `autolink: true` for `https://example.com/foo` even though it directly follows `<`, so a chunk of a non-autolink gets linked and the link text misrepresents what was written (the ` bar>` part is dropped from the link but the visible text suggests the whole bracket was a URL). #4118 covered the `www.` case (``); the protocol case after `<` still links on 18.1.1.
issues.author: philppplik
